page: Alibaba Cloud ecs.u2i-c1m1.8xlarge is an x86_64 server instance provisioned on the KVM hypervisor within the ecs.u2i family. The configuration provides 32 dedicated Intel Xeon vCPUs running at a clock speed of 2.7 GHz. Unlike traditional general-purpose instances that balance compute and memory at wider ratios, this configuration establishes a 1:1 proportion between core count and memory capacity.

The server is equipped with 32.0 GB of system RAM, yielding 1.0 GB of memory per dedicated vCPU. Local storage is completely absent, meaning all persistent storage requires remote network-attached disks. Graphics acceleration is not present, with zero GPUs allocated. Baseline network throughput is rated at 16 Gbps, providing substantial bandwidth for interconnect traffic, while no complimentary public IPv4 addresses are assigned.

From an efficiency standpoint, the dense core allocation relative to system memory provides economic advantages for workloads that are strictly compute-bound. Because tenants do not allocate unused memory overhead, compute density remains resource-efficient. This architecture matches stateless batch processing, distributed worker nodes, continuous integration build runners, and parallel web serving architectures that require significant core capacity without extensive per-thread memory demands.
